Yesterday on a lark I made up a batch of black powder. I made a slurry with whetted ingredients with some powdered sugar to act as a binder so the grains would stay uniform,. I pressed the slurry through a colander (you know that bowl with holes in it so you can that drain vegetables in it) to make up it into grains. I let the grains dry and then loaded them into some .45-70 brass that I had lying around. I then loaded up some 450 grain .458 diameter gas checked lead cast bullets in to my prepped brass. I used 65 grains of my home made black powder because I wasn't sure of he effect of the powdered Sugar in it. Today I took my Springfield model of 1973 .45-70 Trap Door out t behind the barn and fired off 40 rounds of the stuff. it worked pretty well. My chronograph pegged the velocities from 1250 to 1340 fps and the accuracy was pretty good. I got consistent 2 inch (remember that the grouping is outside to outside of the holes farthest apart and a .45-70 had a .458 inch diameter projectile) groups at 100 yards. Because of black powder fouling of the bore the velocities tended to creep up so the groupings tended to be dispersed more vertical than horizontal. But all in all not bad.
